description:
## Goal

Build a greenfield audio-tools scenario that serves as a shared audio microservice for any scenario needing audio capabilities. This is the core deliverable of the continuous-audio-platform initiative.

## P0 Features

### Voice-Session Architecture (transport-pluggable)
- **Voice-session abstraction:** core duplex audio interface — audio in produces transcript events, text in produces TTS audio out. Concrete transports plug into this interface; consumers never depend on a specific transport.
- **Browser-voice transport (ships with greenfield):** WebSocket-based mic + speaker transport for browser consumers. This is the same WebSocket streaming transcription surface previously planned, now declared as a concrete transport rather than the only shape.
- **Future transports (do not ship here):** twilio-voice transport ships separately under phone-agent initiative (execute/audio-tools-twilio-media-stream-transport). Architecture must not preclude SIP/WebRTC/other future transports.
- **Pub/sub event stream:** session events (transcript deltas, assistant deltas, VAD signals, tool events, barge-in cancels) are subscribable by multiple consumers concurrently. Required so a future phone call can be observed live in a browser UI without the observer interfering with the active transport.
- **Barge-in coordination:** VAD signal cancels in-flight TTS audio at the transport AND emits an upstream cancel event so consumers can stop in-flight LLM/agent work.
- **Resampler utilities (P0):** mu-law 8kHz ↔ 16kHz PCM resampling lives in the shared audio-tools package, ready for use by twilio-voice and any other non-browser transport.

### Continuous Voice I/O
- **Streaming transcription:** real-time audio with partial transcription and segment-final retranscription (port from web-console voice_stream_ws.go), surfaced through the browser-voice transport
- **VAD signals:** server-side or client-side voice activity detection with configurable thresholds; emitted on the session event stream
- **Persistent/one-shot modes:** support both always-on listening and single-utterance capture
- **Speaker verification:** optional speaker profile matching per segment

### TTS Pipeline
- **Text-to-speech synthesis:** Kokoro backend with browser TTS fallback
- **Incremental input:** TTS pipeline must accept sentence/chunk deltas (not just full strings) so consumers can stream tokens from upstream LLMs
- **Markdown-to-speech normalization:** transform markdown into speech-friendly text (code blocks → summaries, tables → prose, etc.)
- **Paragraph splitting:** break text into speakable chunks under 4500 chars
- **Pre-synthesis caching:** LRU cache for pre-synthesized audio per event
- **Summarization:** Ollama-based text summarization (light/moderate/heavy levels)

### Audio Processing
- **Format conversion:** MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC, OGG via FFmpeg
- **Editing operations:** trim, merge, split, fade, volume adjustment
- **Normalization and quality enhancement**
- **Metadata extraction**
- **Resampling primitives** (also used by transports — see Voice-Session Architecture)

### Provider Routing
- **Three-tier provider chain** per capability (following BAS pattern):
  - BYOK (user API key for external services)
  - Vrooli/LPBS (subscription-based, credits charged atomically)
  - Local (Whisper, Kokoro, Ollama running on the machine)
- **Per-capability configuration:** different providers for STT, TTS, summarization
- **Credit metering** when routing through LPBS

### Adoption Interface
- **REST API** for audio processing operations
- **WebSocket API** for streaming transcription (this is the browser-voice transport)
- **Voice-session subscription API** for multi-consumer event stream access (UI observer pattern)
- **Adoptable React UI components** that consuming scenarios can embed
- **Configuration inheritance** — consuming scenarios pass their provider preferences

## Architecture

- Go API server (following standard scenario patterns)
- React UI components (embeddable)
- CLI for audio processing operations
- FFmpeg for audio processing
- Provider chain for AI capabilities
- Transport plugin layer over the voice-session interface

## Key References

- Web-console audio implementation: `scenarios/web-console/api/tts_*.go`, `voice_*.go`, `ui/src/hooks/voice/`, `ui/src/hooks/tts/`
- BAS provider chain: `scenarios/browser-automation-studio/api/services/ai/`
- Archived audio-tools docs: `scenarios/swarm-manager/ideas/audio-tools-archived/`
- Voice-session contract source: research/audio-tools-shared-scenario-contract
